Model proposes, Quarry executes: any new action (find, viewport_set, colour scheme) added to AgentAction is also a model-proposable action and needs a risk class (read-only for find, low for emulation); UI-only affordances such as zoom and find need not enter the model allowlist.

Image signing has no CI artifact to sign: Model Plane images are built through a host build script and compose (its compose header), and no workflow pushes Quarry or Model Plane images, so a publish pipeline, registry and key-management decision (Support Plane or infra) must come first; mcp-bridge is not a Quarry component, it is referenced from Model Plane docs and the model-gateway registry. approachAdjustment: Split the bundle. constraints: Model proposes, Quarry executes: WebMCP descriptors discovered in a page are untrusted input and must be fenced, and their execution must go through a Quarry action with a fresh one-shot broker approval grant, never directly from the Model Plane. Child grants must be strict subsets of the parent (ParentGrantID shape) and may never widen the owner's ACL or a Space's authority; the leaf-role rule (agent.rs:1628-1665) must be relaxed only for a defined read-only browser class, not generally. The shared Chromium process means parallel child runs share one browser, and today a UI session (1280x800) and a Model Plane run (no viewport) already force relaunches that drop each other's pages, so that must be fixed before fan-out. ZDR inheritance by child runs was not verified (INF) and must be confirmed before browser children ship.
approachAdjustment: Follow the title: remove site playbooks (F-t2-043) and the MCP exposure wrapper (F-t2-064; the in-loop browser.observe and browser.act aliases already exist) from the summary and approach. For child browser runs: reuse run_delegated_child, add a read-only browser action class to BrowserBroker grants (F-t2-032) with a leaf-role exception limited to that class, add a per-org live-run cap in Quarry, and first make viewport page-scoped so concurrent runs stop relaunching Chromium. Keep WebMCP as a research spike only (the CDP WebMCP domain is experimental, INF) and do not schedule it until real sites publish tools.
